packageRules.description: Group all non-breaking updates into one PR, Sunday, so it is open and green before Monday planning.
One-time digest pinning is mechanical; keep it out of the PR that needs thought.

Ruff is pinned in pyproject.toml and .pre-commit-config.yaml; bump them together. astral-sh/ruff-action is the wrapper's own version, not a Ruff pin: CI resolves Ruff from pyproject.toml via the workflow's version-file input, so it follows the pep621 bump on its own.
Majors are listed on the Dependency Dashboard rather than arriving unannounced.

Upstream carries two tags for the same version, 0.35.0 and v0.35.0 (aquasecurity/trivy-action#573). The collision empties the version set, so every lookup fails with no-result and the action is neither updated nor digest-pinned. Requiring the v prefix makes the unprefixed tag invalid rather than duplicate. Strict by design: a future v0.37 or a pre-release tag would also be excluded, which is the failure mode to check if updates go quiet again.

A Python feature release is a platform upgrade, not a routine bump: docker versioning classifies 3.14 -> 3.15 as a minor. Keeps .python-version and the Dockerfile ARG in lockstep, behind approval. Must stay last; later rules win.
